<context query="Why doesn't Otto use Vertex AI global endpoint for Gemini models" template="default" budget="8000">
<section name="Conventions" source="repo" priority="1">
<document source="specs/support-agent-prompt-and-model/spec.md" type="spec" relevance="1.00" tokens="6">
## Reconciled Decisions
</document>
<document source="README.md" type="doc" relevance="0.99" tokens="761">
## Model

The default is still `mock / in-process`: HAL Engine's mock provider, inside the
api process. A checkout with no `MODEL_ID` and no GCP credential starts on it,
and no data reaches an AI vendor.

The allowlist carries one real row, `gemini-3.1-flash-lite` on Vertex AI, pinned
to the `eu` multi-region. Setting `MODEL_ID=gemini-3.1-flash-lite` runs on it and
makes `GCP_PROJECT_ID` and `VERTEX_LOCATION` required, and `VERTEX_LOCATION` must
be `eu`. The `eu` multi-region is its own host, `aiplatform.eu.rep.googleapis.com`,
which the Vertex SDK does not derive from `location`, so the provider block sets
it as `apiEndpoint` from the region; no setting carries it, and startup refuses a
provider block whose endpoint does not match its row's region. The api
authenticates with Application Default Credentials, so no service-account key
belongs in the environment, the chart or the repository. The row's `evidence` is
provisional: `KU-07` (#7) has not recorded the formal recommendation, and the
NIS-2 Article 21 assessment (#28), the breach-notification clause (#29) and
contractual zero data retention (#30) are all still owed, so the row must not
carry real customer conversations yet.

Measured on 2026-09-23: `gemini-3.1-flash-lite` returns 404 in `europe-west1` and
`europe-north1` and answers only on the `eu` multi-region. It replaces
`gemini-2.5-flash-lite` in `europe-west1`, which Google retires on 20 October 2026.
Gemini 3 models refuse a tool-using turn's next request unless each tool call
comes back with the thought signature it was sent with; `@re-cinq/hal-engine`
0.6.1 carries it (re-cinq/HALEngine#140), so the api needs at least that version.

The `supportAgentProvider` block in `apps/api/src/server.ts` is the single edit
point for the model, and it must match a row of the server-side allowlist in
`apps/api/src/configuration/models.ts` by provider, model and region. At startup
`MODEL_ID` selects the row; unset, it falls back to the default row (`mock`).
An id outside the allowlist, or a provider block that does not match its row,
exits the process before the HTTP port opens. The startup line `api.model`
names the resolved provider, model and region for both the primary and the
fallback (`fallback: none` while `FALLBACK_MODEL_ID` is unset).

`FALLBACK_MODEL_ID` gates a second model for mid-incident failover through the
same allowlist gate as `MODEL_ID`. Absent, the fallback is `none` and a primary
outage stops the agent entirely; set, it must name an allowlist row, or the api
exits before the port opens, and HAL Engine tries it whenever the primary is
unavailable. No credential for the fallback vendor belongs in the environment:
the row's `evidence` names the four artefacts that must exist before a fallback
row is added. Until a fallback vendor is chosen (KU-07), only the mock row can
be the fallback, and only behind the mock: the mock echoes each customer's own
message back, so behind a real model it would answer through that model's
outage. The api refuses both other cases at startup.
</document>

# re:cinq's test environment on the Lore GKE cluster (europe-west1).
# A client installation replaces this file with its own; the chart holds no
# re:cinq-specific default.

pullSecretFromExternalSecret:
  enabled: true
  name: ghcr-pull-secret
  secretStoreRef:
    kind: ClusterSecretStore
    name: gcp-secret-manager
  remoteKey: lore-ghcr-pull-secret

api:
  image:
    repository: ghcr.io/re-cinq/otto-api
  # kubectl create secret generic otto-login --from-literal=username=<name>,<name>,... \
  #   --from-literal=password=...
  loginSecretName: otto-login
  # Every tester gets their own made-up customer, 10001, 10002, ... in the order
  # the Secret lists them. Until the TMS key arrives this environment answers
  # from fixtures; after that a tester may only carry the number of a customer
  # OLT has agreed to test with, so this gives way to customerNumbers pairs.
  firstCustomerNumber: '10001'
  # The stand-in login, served by the api as an OpenID Connect provider (RD-5).
  oidcIssuer: https://otto.gcp.re-cinq.com/api/oauth
  # Made-up bookings of the made-up customers above (#399); live once OLT sends
  # a key (#401).
  tmsMode: 'stand-in'
  # Created by infra/terraform/modules/otto-mongo, which holds the connection
  # string under `url`. Apply infra/terraform/recinq-test before releasing.
  mongoSecretName: otto-mongo
  mongoDbName: otto
  # Vertex AI lives in the cluster's project, on the EU multi-region: on
  # 2026-09-23 gemini-3.1-flash-lite answered on aiplatform.eu.rep.googleapis.com
  # and returned 404 in europe-west1. It replaces gemini-2.5-flash-lite, which
  # Google retires on 2026-10-20. #28, #29 and #30 are still owed, so this environment
  # carries no real customer conversation until they land.
  modelId: gemini-3.1-flash-lite
  gcpProjectId: re5-n8n-platform
  vertexLocation: eu
  # Created by infra/terraform/recinq-test, annotated with
  # otto-api-runtime@re5-n8n-platform.iam.gserviceaccount.com, which holds
  # roles/aiplatform.user and nothing else. Apply that root before releasing.
  serviceAccountName: otto-api
  # No escalationWebhookSecretName: KU-14 has not named a destination, so
  # escalations stay recorded at no_destination_configured.

web:
  image:
    repository: ghcr.io/re-cinq/otto-web

ingress:
  className: nginx-ingress
  host: otto.gcp.re-cinq.com
  annotations:
    cert-manager.io/cluster-issuer: letsencrypt-prod
    external-dns.alpha.kubernetes.io/hostname: otto.gcp.re-cinq.com
    # The chat WebSocket idles between turns; nginx's 60s default would cut it.
    nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/proxy-read-timeout: '3600'
    nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/proxy-send-timeout: '3600'
  tls:
    enabled: true
    secretName: otto-tls

</document>
<document source="specs/support-agent-deployment/spec.md" type="spec" relevance="0.88" tokens="707">
## Out of Scope

- Choosing the model or its region (Lore: `model-evaluation-against-compliance-criteria` (#7), blocked by `KU-07`).
- Setting `api.modelId` to a Vertex row (#253 declares the identity; the change that flips the value is the one that can prove the pod authenticates), and the vendor compliance artefacts that row owes (#7, #28, #29, #30).
- Applying `infra/terraform/recinq-test`. No workflow applies it, and #253 creates nothing in GCP.
- The human IAM bindings of #161 and PR #240: `modules/otto-runtime-identity` is a machine identity and shares no file with the access root.
- The conversation store's own provider and region: [support-agent-conversation-data](../support-agent-conversation-data/spec.md) (#23) picks MongoDB because it does not pin a cloud project. This feature gives its URI a secret and its region a table row; if no EU-resident managed instance is procured before the PoC, the limits document records that the deployment ran on the in-memory store.
- Resuming a conversation across a reconnect or redeploy, which [support-agent-chat](../support-agent-chat/spec.md) adds with #203.
- The end-to-end EU AI Act disclosure assertion (a queued E5 transparency issue).
- Staging and production environments; only `poc` exists. Custom domain mapping, deferred until a domain is agreed and kept separate given the rename incident.
- The vendor-side compliance artefacts (all queued in E5).
- Reading the platform on a schedule, and every non-Cloud-Run asset: [compliance-drift-checks](../compliance-drift-checks/spec.md) (#45) reads every principal and setting from the platform API, and this feature reuses its `planDrift`. A binding made outside terraform is detected there, not here.
- Turning on Data Access audit logs to record who read a conversation ([support-agent-audit-trail](../support-agent-audit-trail/spec.md) (#201)), which also needs a volume and retention decision.
- Access to anything that is not a GCP project: the GitHub repo, the npm org, the model vendor console, OLT's own systems.
- Whether any OLT staff member belongs on the project at all. `KU-18`'s controller/processor split decides that, and no name is added on a guess.
- Moving or recreating CFOAgent's `recinq-cfoagent-terraform-state` bucket (its own migration, with its own risk).
- Whether the Otto root writes secret payloads into state at all (`UU-31`).
- Managing the state bucket itself in terraform. It cannot manage itself, and a committed shell script beats a fourth root with its own local state.
- Customer-managed encryption keys. Every other asset in the residency table uses default Google-managed encryption.
- Whether the api stays internet-reachable once a client portal fronts it (a topology question).
- Any file in `hal-engine`, `bowman-ui` or `cfoagent`.

## Dependencies and Open Questions
</document>

<document source="apps/api/src/configuration/config.ts" type="code" relevance="1.00" tokens="257">
// An id outside the allowlist falls through to resolveModel, which names it and the allowed ids before the port binds.
function readVertexSettings(env: NodeJS.ProcessEnv): VertexSettings | undefined {
  const entry = findModelEntry(env.MODEL_ID);
  if (entry?.providerType !== 'vertex') return undefined;
  enforceExists(
    env.GCP_PROJECT_ID,
    `GCP_PROJECT_ID environment variable is required to run MODEL_ID "${entry.id}" on Vertex AI.`
  );
  enforceExists(
    env.VERTEX_LOCATION,
    `VERTEX_LOCATION environment variable is required to run MODEL_ID "${entry.id}" on Vertex AI.`
  );
  // @google/genai sends a call with no apiEndpoint to this URL, past VERTEX_LOCATION; refused for every row so none inherits it.
  if (env.GOOGLE_VERTEX_BASE_URL?.trim()) {
    throw new Error(
      `GOOGLE_VERTEX_BASE_URL is set, which @google/genai would follow past VERTEX_LOCATION for MODEL_ID "${entry.id}". Unset it.`
    );
  }
  return {projectId: env.GCP_PROJECT_ID, location: env.VERTEX_LOCATION, modelId: entry.id};
}
</document>
<document source="apps/api/src/configuration/models.ts" type="code" relevance="0.97" tokens="163">
// The host, not location, decides where a Vertex request runs, so it must be the one the row's region implies.
function enforceVertexEndpoint(entry: ModelEntry, provider: ProviderConfig): void {
  if (provider.type !== 'vertex') return;
  const expected = vertexApiEndpoint(entry.region);
  if (provider.apiEndpoint === expected) return;
  throw new Error(
    `Model "${entry.id}" in region "${entry.region}" must run on ${describeEndpoint(expected)}, but the provider block runs on ${describeEndpoint(provider.apiEndpoint)}.`
  );
}

export function vertexApiEndpoint(region: string): string | undefined {
  return multiRegionEndpoints.get(region);
}
</document>
</section>
<section name="Architecture Decisions" source="adrs" priority="2">
<document source="adrs/ADR-003-hosting-and-data-residency.md" type="adr" relevance="1.00" tokens="721">
## Context

OLT delegated the platform choice to re:cinq on one condition: the client must know where its data is, fully documented and NIS-2 compliant, because OLT operates in critical infrastructure. In OLT's words, re:cinq must be able to document and prove that data does not leave the controlled hosting environment.

#27 planned Google Cloud Run in `europe-north1`, to sit "in the same region as the Vertex model", and a residency table in `docs/adr/ADR-001-hosting-platform.md`. Neither was built. Otto deploys to the shared GKE cluster instead ([support-agent-deployment](../specs/support-agent-deployment/spec.md) records the divergence), and the premise of the region choice is gone. Measured on 2026-10-16, `europe-north1` serves only the Gemini 2.5 family, which Google retires on 2026-10-20, and the newer Gemini models answer only on the `eu` multi-region ([support-agent-prompt-and-model](../specs/support-agent-prompt-and-model/spec.md), "Region availability, measured"). #27, #162 and #168 are closed as superseded. ADR-001 is the TMS authentication decision (#15), so this record is ADR-003.

## Rejected alternatives

- **Cloud Run in `europe-north1` (#27).** It rested on the model running in `europe-north1`, which no current Gemini model does, and on terraform roots this repository never built.
- **The model's `global` endpoint.** It runs every Gemini model but gives up the EU residency the model allowlist exists to enforce.

## Facts the assessments depend on

- **The project is shared.** `re5-n8n-platform` also runs Lore's cluster, so a human binding there reaches more than Otto.
- **The model row names the EU, not a region.** Inside the `eu` multi-region, Google keeps processing in the EU but picks the region. No Gemini model newer than 2.5 answered in `europe-west1` or `europe-north1` when measured (2026-09-23 and 2026-10-16), and the 2.5 family retires on 2026-10-20.
- **The logs are the one row outside the EU guarantee.** Every other Google Cloud row that holds conversation or personal data is in `europe-west1` or the EU multi-region, but the `_Default` and `_Required` log buckets of `re5-n8n-platform` are `global`. (Outside Google Cloud, the live TMS's region is unknown, KU-01, and it isn't used yet; the container registry holds only code.) The api's own lines carry no conversation content, but they do carry tester names and session ids, which are personal data. A bucket's location can't be changed after creation, so fixing it means a new EU-located bucket with Otto's logs routed to it, or an EU default storage location for the project. The project is shared with Lore, so that is a decision for whoever owns it (see #201 for the related Data Access logs).
- **No customer-managed encryption keys** are configured in `infra/terraform`, `charts/otto` or `deploy/`, so the Google Cloud rows use Google's default encryption at rest.
</document>
</section>
<section name="Agent Memory" source="memories" priority="2">
<document source="dod/otto-273-terraform-description-mechanical" type="memory" tokens="496">
**dod/otto-273-terraform-description-mechanical** (memory): DoD triage for re-cinq/Otto#273 (Name the eu multi-region in the api runtime identity's description) → mechanical, red/green committed & pushed on branch lore/implementation-loop/issue-273.

Key learning for terraform-only tickets in Otto: infra/terraform is NOT exercised by any test suite. CI's `terraform` job (.github/workflows/ci.yml:217-237) runs ONLY `terraform fmt -check -recursive infra/terraform` and, per root, `terraform init -backend=false` + `terraform validate`. No `terraform plan`, no `terraform test`/.tftest.hcl. The Vitest/Playwright suites (.lore/test-commands.yml) never touch infra/. So a change to a planned resource attribute (here google_service_account.runtime.description) has NO honest runnable+CI-judged acceptance seam: the only non-mock red bar is a source-text test (readFileSync main.tf + regex), which the DoD contract forbids. The contract's rule "if the only red bar you can build is a test about source text → mechanical" applies. Name the existing CI fmt/validate checks as the green bar.

terraform binary is NOT preinstalled in the dod pod, but releases.hashicorp.com is reachable — download the CI-pinned version (1.16.2) to /tmp and run fmt -check + validate to honestly quote green. validate needs `init -backend=false` (downloads google ~8.2 / kubernetes ~3.2 providers; light on memory, fine — unlike tsc/eslint which OOM the 1Gi pod). Clean up .terraform dirs and restore recinq-test/.terraform.lock.hcl before committing.

The edit itself: module var `region` (used only in the SA description) renamed to `inference_location`; description reworded to "calls Vertex AI in the ${var.inference_location} multi-region"; recinq-test/main.tf passes inference_location = "eu" while local.region stays europe-west1 for the provider + google_container_cluster lookup. Follow-up to #250 (model moved to gemini-3.1-flash-lite on Vertex eu multi-region aiplatform.eu.rep.googleapis.com).
</document>

- Customer-managed encryption keys. Every other asset in the residency table uses default Google-managed encryption.
- Whether the api stays internet-reachable once a client portal fronts it (a topology question).
- Any file in `hal-engine`, `bowman-ui` or `cfoagent`.

// An id outside the allowlist falls through to resolveModel, which names it and the allowed ids before the port binds.
function readVertexSettings(env: NodeJS.ProcessEnv): VertexSettings | undefined {
  const entry = findModelEntry(env.MODEL_ID);
  if (entry?.providerType !== 'vertex') return undefined;
  enforceExists(
    env.GCP_PROJECT_ID,
    `GCP_PROJECT_ID environment variable is required to run MODEL_ID "${entry.id}" on Vertex AI.`
  );
  enforceExists(
    env.VERTEX_LOCATION,
    `VERTEX_LOCATION environment variable is required to run MODEL_ID "${entry.id}" on Vertex AI.`
  );
  // @google/genai sends a call with no apiEndpoint to this URL, past VERTEX_LOCATION; refused for every row so none inherits it.
  if (env.GOOGLE_VERTEX_BASE_URL?.trim()) {
    throw new Error(
      `GOOGLE_VERTEX_BASE_URL is set, which @google/genai would follow past VERTEX_LOCATION for MODEL_ID "${entry.id}". Unset it.`
    );
  }
  return {projectId: env.GCP_PROJECT_ID, location: env.VERTEX_LOCATION, modelId: entry.id};
}

// The host, not location, decides where a Vertex request runs, so it must be the one the row's region implies.
function enforceVertexEndpoint(entry: ModelEntry, provider: ProviderConfig): void {
  if (provider.type !== 'vertex') return;
  const expected = vertexApiEndpoint(entry.region);
  if (provider.apiEndpoint === expected) return;
  throw new Error(
    `Model "${entry.id}" in region "${entry.region}" must run on ${describeEndpoint(expected)}, but the provider block runs on ${describeEndpoint(provider.apiEndpoint)}.`
  );
}

export function vertexApiEndpoint(region: string): string | undefined {
  return multiRegionEndpoints.get(region);
}

<document source="adrs/ADR-003-hosting-and-data-residency.md" type="adr" relevance="1.00" tokens="721">
## Context

OLT delegated the platform choice to re:cinq on one condition: the client must know where its data is, fully documented and NIS-2 compliant, because OLT operates in critical infrastructure. In OLT's words, re:cinq must be able to document and prove that data does not leave the controlled hosting environment.

#27 planned Google Cloud Run in `europe-north1`, to sit "in the same region as the Vertex model", and a residency table in `docs/adr/ADR-001-hosting-platform.md`. Neither was built. Otto deploys to the shared GKE cluster instead ([support-agent-deployment](../specs/support-agent-deployment/spec.md) records the divergence), and the premise of the region choice is gone. Measured on 2026-10-16, `europe-north1` serves only the Gemini 2.5 family, which Google retires on 2026-10-20, and the newer Gemini models answer only on the `eu` multi-region ([support-agent-prompt-and-model](../specs/support-agent-prompt-and-model/spec.md), "Region availability, measured"). #27, #162 and #168 are closed as superseded. ADR-001 is the TMS authentication decision (#15), so this record is ADR-003.

## Rejected alternatives

- **Cloud Run in `europe-north1` (#27).** It rested on the model running in `europe-north1`, which no current Gemini model does, and on terraform roots this repository never built.
- **The model's `global` endpoint.** It runs every Gemini model but gives up the EU residency the model allowlist exists to enforce.

## Facts the assessments depend on

- **The project is shared.** `re5-n8n-platform` also runs Lore's cluster, so a human binding there reaches more than Otto.
- **The model row names the EU, not a region.** Inside the `eu` multi-region, Google keeps processing in the EU but picks the region. No Gemini model newer than 2.5 answered in `europe-west1` or `europe-north1` when measured (2026-09-23 and 2026-10-16), and the 2.5 family retires on 2026-10-20.
- **The logs are the one row outside the EU guarantee.** Every other Google Cloud row that holds conversation or personal data is in `europe-west1` or the EU multi-region, but the `_Default` and `_Required` log buckets of `re5-n8n-platform` are `global`. (Outside Google Cloud, the live TMS's region is unknown, KU-01, and it isn't used yet; the container registry holds only code.) The api's own lines carry no conversation content, but they do carry tester names and session ids, which are personal data. A bucket's location can't be changed after creation, so fixing it means a new EU-located bucket with Otto's logs routed to it, or an EU default storage location for the project. The project is shared with Lore, so that is a decision for whoever owns it (see #201 for the related Data Access logs).
- **No customer-managed encryption keys** are configured in `infra/terraform`, `charts/otto` or `deploy/`, so the Google Cloud rows use Google's default encryption at rest.
</document>
